components.name: shader-gradient
components.summary: Slow, domain-warped WebGL color field for hero backgrounds; the field bends away from the pointer and content sits on top.

attributes.name: colors
attributes.description: 2 to 5 comma-separated hex colors, dark to light, blended along the field

attributes.name: speed
attributes.description: Flow speed, 0 to 4

attributes.name: grain
attributes.description: Film grain, 0 to 0.3; hides gradient banding

attributes.name: pointer
attributes.description: off stops the field reacting to the pointer

api: data-fallback is set when WebGL is unavailable and the CSS gradient shows instead
notes: Size the element yourself (min-height or aspect-ratio); the canvas fills it at up to 1.5x device pixels.
Pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs, draws one still frame under prefers-reduced-motion, and recovers from a lost WebGL context.
Use one per view: every instance holds its own WebGL context, and browsers allow about 16.

components.name: tilt-card
components.summary: Card that tilts toward the pointer in 3D on a spring, with a moving glare and inner layers that rise toward the viewer.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: Largest tilt in degrees, 0 to 30

attributes.name: scale
attributes.description: Scale while active, 1 to 1.2

attributes.name: glare
attributes.description: Boolean; adds a highlight that follows the pointer

css.name: --mf-tilt-perspective
css.description: Perspective distance; smaller is more dramatic

data.name: data-depth
data.description: On elements inside: pixels the element rises toward the viewer while the card is active

api: refresh() re-reads data-depth elements after you add them
notes: Style the visible card on a child element (the example uses an article); the component rotates a wrapper around it.
Ancestors of data-depth elements get transform-style: preserve-3d. overflow other than visible on those ancestors flattens the depth.
Mouse and pen only, so touch scrolling is never captured; keyboard focus lifts the card without tilting it.

components.name: parallax
components.summary: Layered scroll parallax: each layer moves at its own speed, resting where you laid it out when the section is centered.

data.name: data-speed
data.description: On layers: 1 scrolls normally, 0.5 at half speed (far), 0 stays put, above 1 moves faster (near)

data.name: data-speed-x
data.description: On layers: sideways drift in pixels per scrolled pixel; positive drifts right as you scroll down

notes: Layers move with the translate property, so their own transform is kept.
The section clips its layers (overflow: clip, or hidden in older browsers). Make slow background layers taller than the section (for example inset-block: -30%) so no edge shows.
Listens to scroll only while the section is near the viewport; layers stay still under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: scroll-scene
components.summary: Pinned, scroll-scrubbed stage for motion graphics: CSS reads --mf-progress (0 to 1) and each part's own --mf-p.

attributes.name: length
attributes.description: Scene height in viewports (at least 1); the stage stays pinned for length minus 1 of them

attributes.name: reduced-progress
attributes.description: Progress shown, unpinned, under prefers-reduced-motion

css.name: --mf-progress
css.description: Set on the scene: how far through it the reader has scrolled, 0 to 1

css.name: --mf-p
css.description: Set on each element with data-start or data-end: progress inside that element's window, 0 to 1

data.name: data-start
data.description: Scene progress (0 to 1) where this element's --mf-p starts rising; default 0

data.name: data-end
data.description: Scene progress where this element's --mf-p reaches 1; default 1

api: mf-progress event with detail.progress, fired when progress changes
notes: Drive motion in CSS with calc() on opacity, translate, scale, rotate, or clip-path, for example translate: 0 calc(var(--mf-p) * -40vh).
Write a prefers-reduced-motion rule that shows the whole scene statically; the example stacks its steps.
An ancestor with overflow other than visible breaks position: sticky, and the stage stops pinning.

components.name: reveal
components.summary: Reveals its children one after another as they scroll into view: rise, fade, scale, blur, or clip.

attributes.name: effect
attributes.description: rise, fade, scale, blur, or clip

attributes.name: stagger
attributes.description: Milliseconds between children; children past the twelfth share the last delay

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: Milliseconds per child

attributes.name: repeat
attributes.description: Boolean; hides again when scrolled back above, so it replays

css.name: --mf-reveal-duration
css.description: Transition duration (the duration attribute sets it)

notes: Only direct children animate; wrap groups that should move together.
Hidden children stay in the accessibility tree and print visible.
Load the script in the head so content above the fold doesn't show once before it hides and reveals.

components.name: magnetic
components.summary: Pulls a button toward a nearby pointer on a spring and presses it in on click.

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: Fraction of the pointer's distance from center to follow, 0 to 1

attributes.name: radius
attributes.description: Pixels outside the element where the pull starts

notes: Wrap exactly one button or link; the wrapper moves, so the focus ring moves with it.
Pulls only on devices that hover with a fine pointer, and only while visible. The press stays under prefers-reduced-motion; the pull does not.
Moves with the translate and scale properties, so the child's own transform is kept.

components.name: spotlight
components.summary: One light follows the pointer across a group of cards, lighting each card's border and surface as it passes.
notes: Each direct child is a card: it gets position: relative, and its ::before and ::after are used for the light.
Give cards a border-radius; the light follows it.
Keyboard focus lights the focused card from its center. Touch is ignored.

components.name: text-scramble
components.summary: Text that decodes from shuffling glyphs into its real words, roughly left to right.

attributes.name: trigger
attributes.description: visible (once, when 60% in view), load, or hover (also on keyboard focus)

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: Milliseconds for the whole decode

attributes.name: glyphs
attributes.description: Characters to shuffle through; match the font (digits for numbers, katakana for a Japanese face)

api: text property: set it to decode into new text
notes: Plain text only; markup inside is flattened to its text.
Screen readers and copy-paste get the real text, and the element keeps the final text's size while it runs.
Glyph widths differ in proportional fonts; a monospace font gives the steadiest effect.

components.name: split-text
components.summary: Splits a headline into letters or words that rise, fade, or unblur into place one after another.

attributes.name: by
attributes.description: chars or words

attributes.name: effect
attributes.description: rise (slides up from a mask), fade, or blur

attributes.name: stagger
attributes.description: Milliseconds between units; shortened so the last unit starts within 1.2 s

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: Milliseconds per unit

attributes.name: repeat
attributes.description: Boolean; hides again when scrolled back above, so it replays

api: play() hides the text and reveals it again
notes: Put it inside the heading element, not around it, so the heading keeps its role.
Letters are split by grapheme, so emoji and accented letters stay whole; words never break across lines.
Splitting letters drops kerning between them; use by="words" for body-size text.
